long_biography.plain_text:
William Gordon Bennett returned from wartime naval service and built a furniture-store chain in Arizona. After selling it, an unsuccessful investment cost him much of his capital and led him back into work. Managing casinos for Del Webb taught him the economics of the Nevada resort business before he partnered with William Pennington.

The pair took over struggling Circus Circus and refocused it on value-conscious families, using modest room rates, low-priced food and a separation between children's attractions and the gaming floor. That formula supported new casinos in Reno and Laughlin, followed by the large themed resorts Excalibur and Luxor. Bennett later acquired the Sahara and remained active there until his death in 2002.
